fact: Futarchy is listed as one of Seer's intended application areas, alongside political predictions, food and drugs, macro studies, micro recommendation, and AI markets.

fact: Seer expects its prediction markets to initially appear in a single general purpose frontend.
quote: We expect Seer prediction markets to be initially visible in one general purpose frontend.

fact: Spam and 'tricky' markets—those likely to be invalid or whose literal reading diverges from common understanding—are to be filtered using Kleros Curate, following the Omen precedent.
quote: In order to prevent spam and « tricky » (markets likely to be invalid or markets whose literal interpretation is very different from what most people initially understand) markets, we’ll use Kleros Curate

fact: As the project advances, Seer could support multiple specialised frontends, each addressing a particular use case.
quote: As the project advances, we could have more specialised frontends, each dealing with a special usecase.

fact: Specialised frontends could each have their own governance.
quote: Those could even have their own governance.

fact: Seer aims to be a neutral protocol, meaning contributors may pursue use cases that any given individual does not personally support.
quote: But the idea is for Seer to be a neutral protocol

fact: Neutrality is bounded: the protocol should retain some limits, and abhorrent markets such as assassination markets should not be listed by frontends nor supported by Kleros.
quote: it should still have some limits and abhorrent markets such as assassination markets shouldn’t be listed by frontends nor supported by Kleros

fact: Different contributors contribute to different use cases rather than a single centralized team defining all applications.

fact: Seer is a prediction market platform that uses Reality.eth and the Conditional Tokens Framework to create and manage markets.
quote: Seer is a prediction market platform that leverages Reality.eth and Conditional Tokens Framework to create and manage various types of markets.

fact: Futarchy Markets are a Seer market type intended to support decisions based on a token's predicted price.
quote: Futarchy Markets: To make decisions based on a token’s predicted price.

fact: Categorical markets let users select one outcome from multiple options.
quote: Categorical Markets: Select one out of multiple outcomes.

fact: Multi-categorical markets are similar to categorical markets but allow selecting multiple outcomes.
quote: Multi-Categorical Markets: Similar to categorical market but allowing selection of multiple outcomes.

fact: Scalar markets use a numeric outcome within a specified range.
quote: Scalar Markets: Numeric outcome within a specified range.

fact: Multi-scalar markets involve multiple numeric outcomes.
quote: Multi-Scalar Markets: Multiple numeric outcomes.

fact: Seer uses Reality.eth as its oracle system for resolving market outcomes.
quote: Seer uses Reality.eth as its oracle system for resolving market outcomes.

fact: Questions submitted to Reality.eth include parameters such as opening time, timeout, and minimum bond.
quote: Questions are submitted to Reality.eth with specific parameters such as opening time, timeout, and minimum bond.

fact: Seer supports single-select, multi-select, and numeric scalar question templates.
quote: The system supports multiple question templates, including single-select, multi-select, and numeric (scalar) questions.

fact: Seer uses the Conditional Tokens framework to create and manage outcome tokens.
quote: Seer utilizes the Conditional Tokens framework for creating and managing outcome tokens.

fact: Each market condition is prepared using the Conditional Tokens contract.
quote: Each market condition is prepared using the Conditional Tokens contract.

fact: Outcome tokens are ERC1155 tokens within the Conditional Tokens system.
quote: Outcome tokens are represented as ERC1155 tokens within the Conditional Tokens system.

fact: Seer wraps ERC1155 outcome tokens into ERC20 tokens to improve usability.
quote: To improve usability, Seer wraps the ERC1155 outcome tokens into ERC20 tokens.

fact: Kleros is used to resolve disputes that arise when answering Reality.eth questions.
quote: Seer uses Kleros to resolve disputes that may arise when answering Reality.eth questions.

fact: The documentation navigation lists app and lifecycle actions including create, verify, mint/merge/redeem, buy/sell, report, dispute, resolve, and provide liquidity.
quote: Create a market Verify market Mint, merge, redeem outcome tokens Buy, sell outcome tokens Report answer Raise a dispute Resolve market Provide Liquidity Conditional Markets Futarchy Markets

fact: The system is a decentralized prediction market implementing futarchy governance through token pairs and automated market makers.
quote: A decentralized prediction market system implementing futarchy governance mechanisms using token pairs and automated market makers.

fact: The market uses two token types: currency tokens (SDAI) and company tokens (GNO).
quote:
- Currency Tokens (SDAI)
- Company Tokens (GNO)

fact: Each token type is split into YES and NO positions for taking market-outcome positions.
quote: Each token type is split into YES and NO positions, allowing users to take positions on market outcomes.

fact: YES_SDAI represents a positive currency outcome, while NO_SDAI represents a negative currency outcome.
quote:
YES_SDAI: Represents a positive position on the currency outcome
  - NO_SDAI: Represents a negative position on the currency outcome

fact: YES_GNO represents a positive company outcome, while NO_GNO represents a negative company outcome.
quote:
YES_GNO: Represents a positive position on the company outcome
  - NO_GNO: Represents a negative position on the company outcome

fact: Opening a position involves splitting base tokens into YES/NO pairs.
quote: Users can split base tokens into YES/NO pairs

fact: Closing a position involves merging YES/NO pairs back into base tokens.
quote: Users can merge YES/NO pairs back into base tokens

fact: A surplus is an imbalance between a user's YES and NO tokens.
quote: When a user has an imbalance between YES and NO tokens

fact: Swaps trade between different token types while maintaining position balance.
quote: Trading between different token types while maintaining position balance

fact: The Futarchy Router handles position splitting and merging; the SushiSwap Router executes token swaps.
quote:
- Futarchy Router: Handles position splitting and merging
- SushiSwap Router: Executes token swaps

fact: smartSwap executes token swaps with automatic collateral management, optimal route finding, transaction status tracking, and error handling.
quote:
Executes token swaps with features:
- Automatic collateral management
- Optimal route finding
- Transaction status tracking
- Error handling

fact: closePositions closes surplus positions by calculating available surplus, determining optimal swap pairs, executing balanced swaps, and updating position states.
quote:
Closes surplus positions by:
1. Calculating available surplus
2. Determining optimal swap pairs
3. Executing balanced swaps
4. Updating position states

fact: getPosition provides YES/NO token balances, surplus calculations, and position totals.
quote:
Provides detailed position information:
- YES/NO token balances
- Surplus calculations
- Position totals

fact: canCloseCurrency only allows closing a currency position if the company position has a surplus in the opposite direction.
quote: Checks if currency position can be closed (currency can only be closed if company has surplus in the opposite direction).

fact: UI guidance recommends a dedicated transaction log that shows all steps in sequence with timestamps.
quote:
Implement a dedicated log display that shows all transaction steps in sequence
   - Include timestamps with each log entry
